title: Rama fainted away, after hearing the news of his father's death
introduction: Rama fainted away, after hearing the news of his father's death and is brought back to consciousness by Bharata and others who sprinkle water on him. Rama laments in various ways. Bharata consoles him. Rama in turn consoles Seetha who is weeping. Rama painfully reaches the River Mandakini, offers water and balls of food to the spirit of his departed father and returns to the hut. The crying sounds of those brothers mourning for their dad father with Seetha created and echo in the mountain. Hearing their cry of distress, the troops approach Rama, who receives them all with affection.
closing: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे त्र्युत्तरशततमः सर्गः
Thus completes 103rd Chapter of Ayodhya Kanda of the glorious Ramayana of Valmiki, the work of a sage and the oldest epic.

verses.devanagari:
ताम् श्रुत्वा करुणां वाचं पितुर्मरणसंहिताम् |
राघवो भरतेनोक्तां बभूव गतचेतनः
verses.iast:
tām śrutvā karuṇāṃ vācaṃ piturmaraṇasaṃhitām |
rāghavo bharatenoktāṃ babhūva gatacetanaḥ
verses.translation: Hearing those mournful words relating to the death of his father, spoken by Bharata, Rama fainted away.

verses.devanagari:
तं तु वज्रमिवोत्सृष्टमाहवे दानवारिणा |
वाग्वज्रं भरतेनोक्तममनोज्ञं परम्तपः
प्रगृह्य रामो बाहूवै पुषिताग्रो यथा द्रुमः |
वने परशुना कृत्तस्तथा भुवि पपात ह
verses.iast:
taṃ tu vajramivotsṛṣṭamāhave dānavāriṇā |
vāgvajraṃ bharatenoktamamanojJṇaṃ paramtapaḥ
pragṛhya rāmo bāhūvai puṣitāgro yathā drumaḥ |
vane paraśunā kṛttastathā bhuvi papāta ha
verses.translation: Hearing that unpleasant thunder bolt of words spoken by Bharata, like a thunderbolt released by Indra the Lord of celestials in a battle, Rama the tormentator of his enemies, stretched forth his hands and fell on the ground, in the same manner as a tree covered at extremities with blossoms was cut off by an axe in the forest.

glosses.meaning: by Indra the Lord of celestials

verses.devanagari:
तथा निपतितं रामं जगत्यां जगतीपतिम् |
कूलघातपरिश्रान्तं पसुप्तमिव कुञ्जरम्
भ्रातरस्ते महेष्वासं सर्वतः शोककर्शितम् |
रुदन्तः सह वैदेह्या सिषिभुः सलिलेन वै
verses.iast:
tathā nipatitaṃ rāmaṃ jagatyāṃ jagatīpatim |
kūlaghātapariśrāntaṃ pasuptamiva kuJṇjaram
bhrātaraste maheṣvāsaṃ sarvataḥ śokakarśitam |
rudantaḥ saha vaidehyā siṣibhuḥ salilena vai
verses.translation: Seeing Rama lying on the earth, has the lord of the earth, like an elephant crushed by a land slide on a bank where he was sleeping, those brother along with Seetha approached him from all sides and weepingly sprinkled water on him.

glosses.meaning: and who was the Lord of the world
crushed by a landslide on a bank

verses.devanagari:
स तु संज्ञां पुनर्लब्ध्वा नेत्राभ्यामस्रमुत्सृजन् |
उपाक्रामत काकुत्थ्सः कृपणं बहु भाषितुम्
verses.iast:
sa tu sañjJṇāṃ punarlabdhvā netrābhyāmasramutsṛjan |
upākrāmata kākutthsaḥ kṛpaṇaṃ bahu bhāṣitum
verses.translation: Coming to his senses again and tears falling from his eyes, Rama began to speak much plaintively.

verses.devanagari:
स रामः स्वर्गतं श्रुत्वा पितरम् पृथिवीपतिम् |
उवाच भरतं वाक्यं धर्मात्मा धर्मसंहितम्
verses.iast:
sa rāmaḥ svargataṃ śrutvā pitaram pṛthivīpatim |
uvāca bharataṃ vākyaṃ dharmātmā dharmasaṃhitam
verses.translation: Hearing that the King and his father had ascended to heaven, the virtuous. Rama spoke the following words, consistent with righteousness to Bharata.

verses.devanagari:
किं करिष्याम्ययोध्यायां ताते दिष्टां गतिम् गते |
कस्ताम् राजवराद्धीनामयोध्याम् पालयिष्यति
verses.iast:
kiṃ kariṣyāmyayodhyāyāṃ tāte diṣṭāṃ gatim gate |
kastām rājavarāddhīnāmayodhyām pālayiṣyati
verses.translation: "What should I do with Ayodhya, now that my father reached the end of his life? Who will rule that Ayodhya, which is bereft of that excellent king?

glosses.meaning: gatim = the end of his life?

verses.devanagari:
किम् नु तस्य मया कार्यं दुर्जातेन महात्मनः |
यो मृतो मम शोकेन मया चापि न संस्कृतः
verses.iast:
kim nu tasya mayā kāryaṃ durjātena mahātmanaḥ |
yo mṛto mama śokena mayā cāpi na saṃskṛtaḥ
verses.translation: "In my misfortune, what can I do for that high-souled one? He died of grief on my account and I did not perform the last rites for him!"

glosses.meaning: and not even last rites were performed

verses.devanagari:
अहोः भरत! सिद्धार्थो येन राजा त्वयानुघ!|
शत्रुघ्नेन च सर्वेषु प्रेतकृत्येषु सत्कृतः
verses.iast:
ahoḥ bharata! siddhārtho yena rājā tvayānugha! |
śatrughnena ca sarveṣu pretakṛtyeṣu satkṛtaḥ
verses.translation: "O, Bharata the faultless one! Alas! Happy are you, by whom as well as by Shatrughna the king was honoured by all obsequial rites!"

verses.devanagari:
निष्प्रधाना मनेकाग्रां नरेन्द्रेण विना कृताम् |
निवृत्तवनवासोऽपि नायोध्यां गन्तुमुत्सहे
verses.iast:
niṣpradhānā manekāgrāṃ narendreṇa vinā kṛtām |
nivṛttavanavāso'pi nāyodhyāṃ gantumutsahe
verses.translation: 'Even after the end of my exile, I do not want to return to Ayodhya which is i a disarranged state, deprived of a chief and made bereft of a king."

glosses.meaning: even after the end of my exile
which is in a disarranged state

verses.devanagari:
समाप्तवनवासं मामयोध्यायाम् परम्तप |
कोऽनु शासिष्यति पुनस्तते लोकान्तरं गते
verses.iast:
samāptavanavāsaṃ māmayodhyāyām paramtapa |
ko'nu śāsiṣyati punastate lokāntaraṃ gate
verses.translation: "O, Bharata the tormentator of foes While our father has gone to the other world, who will counsel me when my exile in the forest is over?"

glosses.meaning: when my exile in the forest is over?

verses.devanagari:
पुरा प्रेक्ष्य सुवृत्तं माम् पिता यान्याह सान्त्वयन् |
वाक्यानि तानि श्रोष्यामि कुतः श्रोतसुखान्यहम्
verses.iast:
purā prekṣya suvṛttaṃ mām pitā yānyāha sāntvayan |
vākyāni tāni śroṣyāmi kutaḥ śrotasukhānyaham
verses.translation: "Formerly, seeing my good conduct, our father used to address me in words of praise; from whom now shall I hear those words delightful to the ears?"

glosses.meaning: which are delightful to the ears?

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्त्वा स भरतं भार्यामभ्येत्य राघवः |
उवाच शोकसम्तप्तः पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम्
verses.iast:
evamuktvā sa bharataṃ bhāryāmabhyetya rāghavaḥ |
uvāca śokasamtaptaḥ pūrṇacandranibhānanām
verses.translation: Having spoken thus to Bharata, Rama went to seek out his consort, whose face resembled the full moon, and overwhelmed with grief, spoke to her as follows:-

glosses.meaning: whose face was like a full moon

verses.devanagari:
सीते मृतस्ते श्वशुरः पित्रा हीनोऽसि लक्ष्मण |
भरतो कुःखमाचष्टे स्वर्गतं पृथिवीपतिम्
verses.iast:
sīte mṛtaste śvaśuraḥ pitrā hīno'si lakṣmaṇa |
bharato kuḥkhamācaṣṭe svargataṃ pṛthivīpatim
verses.translation: "O, Seetha! your father-in-law is dead. O, Lakshmana! You have become bereft of your father. Bharata is informing a sorrowful news of the emperor being dead.

verses.devanagari:
ततो बहुगुणम् तेषां बाष्पो नेत्रेष्वजायत |
तथा ब्रुवति काकुत्थ्स कुमाराणां यशस्विनाम्
verses.iast:
tato bahuguṇam teṣāṃ bāṣpo netreṣvajāyata |
tathā bruvati kākutthsa kumārāṇāṃ yaśasvinām
verses.translation: While Rama was uttering those words, copious tears caused to flow then from the eyes of those sons of Dasaratha.

glosses.meaning: from the eyes of those illustrious sons of Dasaratha.

verses.devanagari:
ततस्ते भ्रातरस्सर्वे भृशमाश्वास्य राघवम् |
अब्रुवन् जगतीभर्तुः क्रियतामुदकं पितुः
verses.iast:
tataste bhrātarassarve bhṛśamāśvāsya rāghavam |
abruvan jagatībhartuḥ kriyatāmudakaṃ pituḥ
verses.translation: Then, all those brothers consoled Rama very much and said to him, "Let us offer libations of water for our father, the Lord of the earth."

verses.devanagari:
सा सीता श्वशुरं श्रुत्वा स्वर्गलोकगतम् नृपम् |
नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यामशकन्नेक्षितुं पतिम्
verses.iast:
sā sītā śvaśuraṃ śrutvā svargalokagatam nṛpam |
netrābhyāmaśrupūrṇābhyāmaśakannekṣituṃ patim
verses.translation: Hearing that her father-in-law, that great monarch had ascended to heaven, Seetha was unable to see her husband through eyes filled with tears.

verses.devanagari:
सान्त्वयित्वा तु तां रामो रुदतीं जनकात्मजाम् |
उवाच लक्ष्मणम् तत्र दुःखितो दुःखितम् वचः
verses.iast:
sāntvayitvā tu tāṃ rāmo rudatīṃ janakātmajām |
uvāca lakṣmaṇam tatra duḥkhito duḥkhitam vacaḥ
verses.translation: Rama consoled that Seetha who was weeping and himself stricken with grief, spoke to the lamenting Lakshmana as follows:

verses.devanagari:
आनयेङ्गुदिपिण्याकं चीरमाहर चोत्तरम् |
जलक्रियार्थं तातस्य गमिष्यामि महात्मनः
verses.iast:
ānayeṇ^gudipiṇyākaṃ cīramāhara cottaram |
jalakriyārthaṃ tātasya gamiṣyāmi mahātmanaḥ
verses.translation: "Bring the crushed pulp of Ingudi Tree and bring a piece of bark for being wrapped about my loins and another for being used as my loins and another for being used as an upper garment, so that we may proceed to offer libations of water for our magnanimous father."

glosses.meaning: the crushed pulp of Ingudi Tree
a piece of bark for being wrapped about my loins
and another for being used as an upper garment

verses.devanagari:
सीता पुरस्ताद्र्वजतु त्वमेनामभितो व्रज |
अहं पश्चाद्गमिष्यामि गति र्ह्येषा सुदारुणा
verses.iast:
sītā purastādrvajatu tvamenāmabhito vraja |
ahaṃ paścādgamiṣyāmi gati rhyeṣā sudāruṇā
verses.translation: "Let Seetha walk in the front and you follow after her nearby. I shall follow in the rear. This indeed is the most terrible procession.

verses.devanagari:
ततो नित्यानुगस्तेषां विदितात्मा महामतिः |
मृदुर्दान्तस्च शान्तश्च रामे च दृढभक्तिमान्
सुमन्त्रस्तैर्नृपसुतैः सार्धमाश्वास्य रागवम् |
आवातारयदालम्ब्य नदीम् मन्दाकिनीम् शिवाम्
verses.iast:
tato nityānugasteṣāṃ viditātmā mahāmatiḥ |
mṛdurdāntasca śāntaśca rāme ca dṛḍhabhaktimān
sumantrastairnṛpasutaiḥ sārdhamāśvāsya rāgavam |
āvātārayadālambya nadīm mandākinīm śivām
verses.translation: Then, their faithful companion Sumantra versed in the spiritual science, endowed with great intelligence, kind, self-controlled and glorious, and deeply devoted to Rama, consoling him and his brothers, took Rama by the hand and helped him descend to the auspicious River Mandakini.

verses.devanagari:
ते सुतीर्थाम् ततः कृच्छ्रादुपागम्य यशस्विनः |
नदीम् मन्दाकिनीम् रम्याम् सदा पुष्पितकाननाम्
शीघ्रश्रोतसमासाद्य तीर्थम् शिममकर्दमम् |
सिषिचुस्तुदकं राज्ञे तातैतत्ते भवत्विति
verses.iast:
te sutīrthām tataḥ kṛcchrādupāgamya yaśasvinaḥ |
nadīm mandākinīm ramyām sadā puṣpitakānanām
śīghraśrotasamāsādya tīrtham śimamakardamam |
siṣicustudakaṃ rājJṇe tātaitatte bhavatviti
verses.translation: The illustrious Rama and others painfully reached the River Mandakini, that stream of sacred fords, the enchanting one always covered with flowers, coming to a blessed ford, free from mud and offered the lustrual water to the king, saying "Father! May this prove agreeable to you."

verses.devanagari:
प्रगृह्य च महीपालो जलपूरितमञ्जलिम् |
दिशम् याम्यामभिमुखो रुदन्वचनम्ब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
pragṛhya ca mahīpālo jalapūritamaJṇjalim |
diśam yāmyāmabhimukho rudanvacanambravīt
verses.translation: Holding together in the form of a hollow his palms full of water and turning his face turned towards the southern quarter and weeping the great prince pronounced the traditional words saying:

glosses.meaning: in the form of a hollow his palms
and turning his face turned towards

verses.devanagari:
एतत्ते राजशार्दूल विमलं तोयमक्षयम् |
पितृलोकगतस्याद्य मद्दत्तमुपतिष्ठतु
verses.iast:
etatte rājaśārdūla vimalaṃ toyamakṣayam |
pitṛlokagatasyādya maddattamupatiṣṭhatu
verses.translation: O, Tiger among men! May this water without taint and incorruptible at the moment that I offer it to you, reach you in the region of your ancestors where you are."

glosses.meaning: in the region of your ancestors where you are.

verses.devanagari:
ततो मन्दाकिनीतीरात्र्पत्युत्तीर्य स राघवः |
पितुश्चकार तेजस्वी निवापं ब्रातृभिः सह
verses.iast:
tato mandākinītīrātrpatyuttīrya sa rāghavaḥ |
pituścakāra tejasvī nivāpaṃ brātṛbhiḥ saha
verses.translation: Thereafter, the glorious Rama, resending the bank of Mandakini River along with his brothers, offered balls of food to his father.

verses.devanagari:
ऐङ्गुदम् बदरीमिश्रम् पिण्याकम् दर्भसंस्तरे |
न्यस्य रामस्स दुःखार्तो रुदन्वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
aiṇ^gudam badarīmiśram piṇyākam darbhasaṃstare |
nyasya rāmassa duḥkhārto rudanvacanamabravīt
verses.translation: Rama placed the pulp of the Ingudi tree mixed with the pulp of plums on a mat of Kusa grass and overcome with sadness, weeping, spoke the following words:

glosses.meaning: the pulp of the Ingudi tree
on a mat of kusa grass

verses.devanagari:
इदम्भुङ्क्ष्व महाराज प्रीतो यदशना वयम् |
यदन्नः पुरुषो भवति तदन्ना स्तस्य देवताः
verses.iast:
idambhuṇ^kṣva mahārāja prīto yadaśanā vayam |
yadannaḥ puruṣo bhavati tadannā stasya devatāḥ
verses.translation: "O, Great King! Be pleased to partake of this, which we eat for, that which man eats, is also consumed by his gods."

verses.devanagari:
ततस्तेनैव मार्गेण प्रत्युत्तीर्य नदीतटात् |
आरुरोह नरव्याघ्रो रम्यसानुं महिधरम्
verses.iast:
tatastenaiva mārgeṇa pratyuttīrya nadītaṭāt |
āruroha naravyāghro ramyasānuṃ mahidharam
verses.translation: Rama the tiger among men then re-ascending by the same path on the banks of the river reached the charming summit of Chitrakuta mountain.

glosses.meaning: on the banks of the river

verses.devanagari:
ततः पर्णकुटीद्वारमासाद्य जगतीपतिः |
परिजग्राह बाहुभ्यामुभौ भरतलक्ष्मणौ
verses.iast:
tataḥ parṇakuṭīdvāramāsādya jagatīpatiḥ |
parijagrāha bāhubhyāmubhau bharatalakṣmaṇau
verses.translation: Gaining the door of his leafy hut, Rama the Lord of the earth then embraced Bharata and Lakshmana with his arms.

glosses.meaning: Rama the Lord of the earth
the door of his leafy hut

verses.devanagari:
तेषां तु रुदतां शब्दात्प्रतिश्रुत्कोऽभवद्गिरौ |
भ्रात्ऱ्^ऊ सह वैदेह्या सिंहानामिव नर्धताम्
verses.iast:
teṣāṃ tu rudatāṃ śabdātpratiśrutko'bhavadgirau |
bhrātR^ū saha vaidehyā siṃhānāmiva nardhatām
verses.translation: From the sound of the cry of those brothers with Seetha, which resembled like the roaring of lions rose an echo in the mountain.

verses.devanagari:
महाबलानाम् रुदताअं कुर्वतामुदकं पितुः |
विज्ञाय तुमुलं शब्दम् त्रस्ता भरतसैनिकाः
verses.iast:
mahābalānām rudatāaṃ kurvatāmudakaṃ pituḥ |
vijJṇāya tumulaṃ śabdam trastā bharatasainikāḥ
verses.translation: Hearing the tumultuous clamour by those mighty heroes as, weeping they completed the libations of water to their father, Bharata's army got alarmed.

verses.devanagari:
आब्रुवंश्चापि रामेण भरतस्संगतो ध्रुवम् |
तेषामेव महाशब्दः शोचतां पितरं मृतम्
verses.iast:
ābruvaṃścāpi rāmeṇa bharatassaṅgato dhruvam |
teṣāmeva mahāśabdaḥ śocatāṃ pitaraṃ mṛtam
verses.translation: Those troops of Bharata also said, "Assuredly, Bharata has joined Rama and this is a great sound only of their wailing, as they mourn for their dead father."

verses.devanagari:
अथ वासान्परित्यज्य तं सर्वेऽभिमुखाः स्वनम् |
अ प्येकमनसो जग्मुर्यथास्थानम् प्रधाविताः
verses.iast:
atha vāsānparityajya taṃ sarve'bhimukhāḥ svanam |
a pyekamanaso jagmuryathāsthānam pradhāvitāḥ
verses.translation: Leaving their tents all of them having but one thought, went running in the direction of that sound instantly.

verses.devanagari:
हयैरन्ये गजैरन्ये रथैरन्ये स्वलम्कृतैः |
सुकुमारास्तथैवान्ये पद्भिरेव नरा ययः
verses.iast:
hayairanye gajairanye rathairanye svalamkṛtaiḥ |
sukumārāstathaivānye padbhireva narā yayaḥ
verses.translation: Some went on their horses, some others on their elephants, some in their chariots covered with ornaments while the youthful people went on foot.

verses.devanagari:
अचिरप्रोषितम् रामम् चिरविप्रोषितं यथा |
द्रष्टुकामो जनस्सर्वो जगाम सहसाश्रमम्
verses.iast:
aciraproṣitam rāmam ciraviproṣitaṃ yathā |
draṣṭukāmo janassarvo jagāma sahasāśramam
verses.translation: In their longing to see Rama, whose absence though recent, seemed so long a period for them, the whole people ran towards the hermitage.

verses.devanagari:
भ्रात्ऱूणां त्वरितास्तत्र द्रष्टुकामास्समागमम् |
युयुर्बहुविधैर्यानैः खरनेविस्वनाकुलैः
verses.iast:
bhrātRūṇāṃ tvaritāstatra draṣṭukāmāssamāgamam |
yuyurbahuvidhairyānaiḥ kharanevisvanākulaiḥ
verses.translation: Eager to see those brothers re-united there, they went hastily by various means of transport, either by hoofed animals or by wheeled vehicles.

glosses.meaning: like hoofed animals and wheeled vehicles.

verses.devanagari:
सा भूमिर्बहुभिर्यानै खरनेमिसम्रहता |
मुमोच तुमुलं शब्दं द्यौरिवाभ्रसमागमे
verses.iast:
sā bhūmirbahubhiryānai kharanemisamrahatā |
mumoca tumulaṃ śabdaṃ dyaurivābhrasamāgame
verses.translation: Trodden by many vehicles, beasts and chariots, that land emitted a tumultuous noise, as a sky during the conjunction of clouds.

verses.devanagari:
तेन वित्रासिता नागाः करेणुपरिवारिताः |
आवासयन्तो गन्धेन जग्मुरन्यद्वनम् ततः
verses.iast:
tena vitrāsitā nāgāḥ kareṇuparivāritāḥ |
āvāsayanto gandhena jagmuranyadvanam tataḥ
verses.translation: Frightened by that noise, the wild elephants, surrounded by female elephants, perfuming the quarters with teh scent of their ichor, went to another wood from there.

glosses.meaning: with the scent of their ichor

verses.devanagari:
वराहवृकसम्घाश्च सिंहाश्च महिषाः सर्पवानराः |
व्याघ्रगोकर्णगवयाः वित्रेसुः पृषतैस्सह
verses.iast:
varāhavṛkasamghāśca siṃhāśca mahiṣāḥ sarpavānarāḥ |
vyāghragokarṇagavayāḥ vitresuḥ pṛṣataissaha
verses.translation: Boars, wolves and lions, buffaloes, snakes, monkeys, tigers, Gokarnas and Gavayas (two distinctive species of deer) along with spotted deer felt frightened.

verses.devanagari:
रथाङ्गसाह्वा नत्यूह हंसाः कारण्डवाः प्लवाः |
तथा पुंस्कोकोलाः क्रौञ्च विसम्ज्ञा भेजिरे दिशः
verses.iast:
rathāṇ^gasāhvā natyūha haṃsāḥ kāraṇḍavāḥ plavāḥ |
tathā puṃskokolāḥ krauJṇca visamjJṇā bhejire diśaḥ
verses.translation: The ruddy gooses, water-fowls, swans, Karandavas ( a sort of ducks), herons, male cuckoos and cranes, utterly confused made it to various directions.

verses.devanagari:
तेन शब्देन वित्रस्तैराकासं पक्षिभिर्वऋतम् |
मनुष्यैरावृता भूमिरुभयम् प्रबभौ त दा
verses.iast:
tena śabdena vitrastairākāsaṃ pakṣibhirvaṛtam |
manuṣyairāvṛtā bhūmirubhayam prababhau ta dā
verses.translation: The sky filled with birds that had been frightened by that noise and the earth covered with men, both looked beautiful at that moment.

verses.devanagari:
तत्तस्तं पुरुषव्याघ्रम् यशस्विन मकीलम्षम् |
आसीनं स्थण्डिले रामम् ददर्श सहसा जनः
verses.iast:
tattastaṃ puruṣavyāghram yaśasvina makīlamṣam |
āsīnaṃ sthaṇḍile rāmam dadarśa sahasā janaḥ
verses.translation: Suddenly then, the people beheld the illustrious and the sinless Rama, sitting on the bare earth.

verses.devanagari:
विगर्हमाणः कैकेयीं मन्थरासहितामपि |
अभिगम्य जनो रामम् बाष्पपूर्णमुखोऽभवत्
verses.iast:
vigarhamāṇaḥ kaikeyīṃ mantharāsahitāmapi |
abhigamya jano rāmam bāṣpapūrṇamukho'bhavat
verses.translation: Abusing Kaikeyi and Manthara, those people turned up with their faces bathed in tears. while approaching Rama.

glosses.meaning: with their faces bathed in tears

verses.devanagari:
तान्नरान् बाष्पपूर्णाक्षान् समीक्ष्यथ सुदुःखितान् |
पर्यष्वजत धर्मज्ञः पितृवन्मातृवच्च नः
verses.iast:
tānnarān bāṣpapūrṇākṣān samīkṣyatha suduḥkhitān |
paryaṣvajata dharmajJṇaḥ pitṛvanmātṛvacca naḥ
verses.translation: Seeing those people thus deeply afflicted their eyes suffused with tears, Rama knowing what was right, embraced them like their father and mother.

verses.devanagari:
स तत्र कांश्चित् परिषन्वजे नरान् |
नराश्च केचित्तु तमभ्यवादयन् |
चकार सर्वान् सवयस्यबान्धवान् |
यथार्ह मासाद्य तदा नृपात्मजः
verses.iast:
sa tatra kāṃścit pariṣanvaje narān |
narāśca kecittu tamabhyavādayan |
cakāra sarvān savayasyabāndhavān |
yathārha māsādya tadā nṛpātmajaḥ
verses.translation: Rama embraced some men there, while some others offered salutations to him. Approaching them on that occasion, the king's son received them all including his friends and companions.

verses.devanagari:
स तत्र तेषाम् रुदतां महात्मनां |
भुवम् ब खम् चाशुनिनादयन् स्वनः |
गुह गिरीणाम् च दिश्श्च सन्ततं |
मृदङ्गघोषप्रतिमः प्रशुश्रुवे
verses.iast:
sa tatra teṣām rudatāṃ mahātmanāṃ |
bhuvam ba kham cāśuninādayan svanaḥ |
guha girīṇām ca diśśca santataṃ |
mṛdaṇ^gaghoṣapratimaḥ praśuśruve
verses.translation: The tumult of those magnanimous persons lamenting, resounded over the earth and in the sky, reverberating through the mountain caves and in all quarters like the continuous beating of drums.
